category_title: Average-level readers engaging in balanced discourse
minimal_context: The student is identifying the author's message in a book about a boy and chocolate during a one-on-one reading conference.
dialogue:
TUTOR: What is the author's message in this book about the boy and the chocolate?

STUDENT: I think the author’s message is, um, you should ask permission before you get something.

TUTOR: Okay. Anything else?

STUDENT: Well, his mom said he’s not allowed to eat any more chocolate.

TUTOR: Go on.

STUDENT: He just kept eating chocolate over and over until he went to the doctor's and they said he had a chocolate disease. I don't know how else to explain the message.

options.A: Teach the student a placeholder strategy of reading the first letter of a word instead of the entire word as long as they understand.
options.B: Follow the student's lead rather than following a set curriculum and setting out to explicitly 'teach' them something during the conference.
options.C: Pay attention to the student's avoidance strategies as compensations rather than refusals to comply with the expected reading conference task.
options.D: Invite the student to talk about their book and respond to questions using SEM-R bookmarks with sample higher-level and follow-up questions.
